description: The bar chart illustrates percent-point differences for two multilingual BERT models across several hidden-layer configuration categories. The horizontal axis contains four categorical settings in left-to-right order: “hidden:[50], linear,” “hidden:[], linear,” “hidden:[100], ReLU,” and “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU.” The vertical axis is labeled “% point difference” and uses a linear scale spanning approximately from −0.2 to 0.2, with regularly spaced tick marks at about 0.1 intervals (−0.2, −0.1, 0.0, 0.1, 0.2). Each category shows a pair of side-by-side bars corresponding to the legend in the upper right: mBERT (lighter gray-blue) and XLM-R (darker blue). For “hidden:[50], linear,” the mBERT bar is near −0.20 and the XLM-R bar is around −0.06; for “hidden:[], linear,” mBERT is about +0.09 and XLM-R is about +0.21; for “hidden:[100], ReLU,” mBERT is around −0.11 and XLM-R is slightly above zero at roughly +0.03; and for “hidden:[50, 50], ReLU,” mBERT is near −0.18 and XLM-R is around −0.14. The bars are grouped by category (two bars per group), there is no stacking, and there are no visible annotations or special emphasis beyond the color coding; the categories do not appear to be sorted by bar height.
